"They don’t want to increase the minimum wage, which would eventually push up pay for everyone else as well." How? How would a minimum wage increase pay for other jobs?

Because a lot of jobs base their salaries off minimum wage.

People don't realize that if EVERYONE got a raise, then sure, things would be rough for the corporate entity supporting them. But then, with this extra money people are making... They'll spend more! Which then will make these corporations more money.

Whenever anyone cries that a high minimum wage stifles correlate growth, just remember. Costco pays their people 30-50 G a year. Great benefits,etc.

These people spend the majority of their money at Costco! It's the perfect system.

The best illustration was Gravity Payments.

This company raised all wage levels to $70 K per year. This created resentment for those that didn't receive a bump (as well as for those who received lesser raises) and a large number have left taking their experience elsewhere to find higher wages. If the experiment were to start at the bottom with a bump in lowest paid workers (i.e. raise minimum wage) the employer will have to decide if a new scale across the board for everyone is needed in order to keep skilled and experienced people (who earn more now) from jumping ship and finding employment elsewhere.

Anyone with ambition will always be weighing their worth to an organization against their loyalty to that organization. An across the board bump in the minimum wage only hurts those businesses that view employees as "drones" without any special skills. They have automated their businesses to the point that they feel they don't need experience or skills (Fast Food chains and Wal-Mart are two examples that come to mind.) The effect on these businesses will ripple through the businesses who will still find ways to lower overall business costs to maintain the current profit levels. (Do you honestly think that "self checkout" wouldn't exist if there wasn't a minimum wage?)
